operationalization: On logged cell-state time series from the evolved French-flag network, compute pairwise local transfer entropy between red and white stripe cells with history k = 4, as defined in the paper. A red-to-white peak before about step 60 followed by a larger white-to-red peak confirms the reported reversal; no reversal, or a reversal that disappears under alternate binning, refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public Python implementation of the evolved French-flag tissue; the committed tree does not include winner_net.txt or the logged trajectories

candidate_datasets.name: Java Information Dynamics Toolkit
candidate_datasets.role: standard library for the local transfer entropy the paper uses to compare stripes

obstacles: The published winner network and cell-state time series are not in the repository, and the committed run.py uses a two-generation demonstration setting.
Transfer entropy is computed on one representative individual; stripe-to-stripe sums are confounded by which cells are actually changing state.
Directed information flow is not a graft assay, so it does not show that a stripe instructively induces pattern in the other.
rationale: The information-theoretic contrast is specified tightly enough, and the model code is public, that recomputing stripe-to-stripe transfer entropy is analysis rather than a new experiment. What is missing is the evolved network and the traces behind the published peaks, so a re-evolution tests whether the reversal is a typical output, not whether the reported run had it. The organizer reading remains a gloss on that asymmetry.

operationalization: Average local transfer entropy from each cell's energy to its state, and the reverse, across the tissue time series. An energy-to-state peak near step 55 that precedes overlap of the two directions would confirm the reported order; a first peak in the opposite direction, or simultaneous rise, would refute the order.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public model in which energy and cell state are explicit variables; saved analysis trajectories are not deposited

candidate_datasets.name: Java Information Dynamics Toolkit
candidate_datasets.role: implementation of local transfer entropy between energy and cell state

obstacles: Saved energy and state traces for the reported run are not in the code repository.
A lead of energy-to-state transfer entropy is compatible with a common driver and does not establish top-down control of survival energy.
rationale: The peak-order comparison can be rerun once energy and state are logged from the public model, using the paper's definition of local transfer entropy. The deposited code does not include those logs or the winner network, and the further statement that the anatomical loop controls single-cell energy is not identified by peak order alone. A re-evolved tissue can test the qualitative order, not the published figure.

operationalization: Plot mean local active information storage of cell state against stress in the same runs, with stress discretized in chunks of 10. Stress rising while active information storage of the white and red stripes falls, then the reverse as stress falls, would confirm the reported concurrence; stress spikes with flat or rising storage would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public simulation with explicit stress and cell-state variables; the information-storage analysis itself is not implemented in the repository

candidate_datasets.name: Java Information Dynamics Toolkit
candidate_datasets.role: library for local active information storage on the cell-state series

obstacles: The blue stripe has zero active information storage because those cells never change state, so the tissue average is structurally biased.
The reported concurrence is from a representative run, and the winner network is not deposited.
rationale: Stress and active information storage are defined quantitatively, so their timing can be recomputed from logged runs of the public model. The repository does not contain the analyzed trajectories, and the evolutionary claim that stress was recruited as a channel for failed prediction is an interpretation of a correlation. Re-evolution would speak to whether the correlation is typical.

operationalization: Follow individual regenerating or developing animals after an apparently stable phenotype and record whether anatomy changes again without a new intervention, using the planarian cutoff of any morphology change after four weeks. Repeated independent cohorts in which a non-trivial fraction remodel after long stability would support the prediction; large cohorts followed well past that window with no late change would count against it.
obstacles: The wording is that something similar may occur, so failure to see late remodelling does not refute it.
No public animal-level longitudinal morphology table covers the weeks after apparent regenerative completion.
Late change can be produced by starvation, infection, or residual drug rather than an intrinsic return to an anatomical trajectory.
rationale: The planarian version of the prediction is measurable, but the only quantitative series is this paper's own aggregate, and the supplementary file is a document of figures rather than a reusable cohort table. Independent long-term imaging after a scored stable phenotype is not in a public dataset. Re-reading the paper's figure is not a test of the prediction.

operationalization: Score each Dugesia japonica pre-tail fragment treated with 18 μM U0126 for three days, kept individually until death, for any morphology change after four weeks, and among those for return to one head. A recount near 22% of about 181 animals, mostly between four and ten weeks, with about 61% of the changers restoring one head, would confirm the report; a recount far from those fractions, or an independent cohort at the same dose with almost no late change, would refute it.
obstacles: Animal-level weekly scores are not deposited; the public record is the summary and figure 10.
The scoring rubric counts fission and dorsal or lateral outgrowths as repatterning, and fission creates a new wound.
Headless animals cannot feed, so late change is confounded with prolonged starvation.
rationale: The dose, fragment type, follow-up, and phenotype classes are explicit, so a recount would decide the percentages. Those worm-by-worm scores are not in a public table, and the figshare supplement is a supplementary document rather than the scoring sheet. Without that sheet or an independent cohort, the published summary cannot be checked.

operationalization: Compare the latency from completed regeneration to spontaneous anatomical change in ERK-inhibited headless Dugesia with the published time to a stable regenerate in untreated fragments of the same species. Latencies of many weeks, well beyond the usual one-to-two-week regenerative window, would support a slower tissue process; latencies inside the ordinary window, or late changes explained by drug persistence or starvation, would count against it.
obstacles: The latency distribution is not available as a public individual-level table.
A slow residual effect of U0126, or injury from late fission, mimics a newly discovered slow tissue process.
rationale: A timescale comparison is well posed only if the late-change events and a baseline regenerative schedule can be aligned animal by animal. The late events are not deposited beyond the paper's summary, so the inference to an unknown slow process cannot be separated from drug, wound, or starvation alternatives with existing public records.

operationalization: In runs of the evolved tissue, measure distance to the French-flag target over time and read the fitness function in the code. A transient increase in distance while misplaced cells are removed, followed by return, in a model whose fitness does not reward that excursion or long-term maintenance, would support the simulation result; monotonic approach, or a fitness term that penalizes intermediate error, would refute the unselected-excursion reading.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public evolutionary model whose fitness evaluation and tissue dynamics can be inspected; paper hyperparameters and winner networks are not committed

obstacles: Whether intermediate error is invisible to selection depends on whether fitness is an endpoint score or a time integral, which has to be read out of the model class rather than a deposited results table.
The committed script is a short demonstration configuration, so it is not a replay of the published 1000-step runs.
rationale: The excursion away from the target and the contents of the fitness function can be checked by running and reading the public model, which is analysis. The repository does not contain the published long runs, and the step from this fitness function to unselected capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems generally is outside what one simulation decides. Endpoint versus cumulative fitness is a real ambiguity in the test.

operationalization: Classify each late planarian morphology change by whether a new wound, fission, or bite occurred in the preceding interval. Events with no wound would support initiation without a missing-tissue response; restriction of late heads to post-fission wounds would count against it.
obstacles: The paper's own repatterning classes include fission, which opens a wound, and those classes are not deposited animal by animal.
A possibility claim that a missing-tissue response may be unnecessary is weakly refutable.
rationale: Whether a new injury preceded each late regenerative event is decidable from longitudinal notes, and those notes are not public. The aggregate result mixes fission with other morphology changes, so the existing summary does not separate regeneration-without-injury from regeneration-after-a-late-wound. A general claim about the missing-tissue response needs cohorts beyond this experiment.

operationalization: Compare published bacterial biofilm stress oscillations, vertebrate segmentation-clock time series, and stress-linked stripe formation in the French-flag model for a shared motif in which a metabolic or stress oscillation sets spatial boundaries. A common motif under a pre-specified distance on those series would support a shared dynamical pattern; qualitatively different mechanisms would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public kinetic models of segmentation clocks and other spatial oscillators, for a dynamical comparison rather than a homology test

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: time-resolved expression series during somitogenesis that can be compared with oscillator models

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: the in silico stress-and-stripe system named in the comparison

obstacles: Shared oscillation-plus-pattern is compatible with analogy and does not show a conserved mechanism from bacteria to metazoans.
No single public dataset pairs biofilm nitrogen stress, vertebrate segmentation, and the neural cellular automaton under one schema.
rationale: Pieces of the comparison are public: segmentation-clock models and expression series, and the tissue simulation. They can test a restricted dynamical resemblance. They do not contain a cross-kingdom homology or a matched stress-to-pattern experiment, so the conservation reading stays underdetermined.

operationalization: A non-cognitive description, in which the same ion channels, stresses, and gene-regulatory loops implement physiological homeostasis at cell and tissue scale, predicts the same developmental and regenerative observations. No public measurement separates retained ancestral cognition scaled to anatomical goals from that physiological description, so there is no confirming or refuting outcome.
obstacles: Cognitive repertoire and anatomical goals have several contested operationalizations.
Comparative presence of ancient cell-biological machinery does not decide whether that machinery is cognition.
rationale: The historical and cognitive wording does not add an observation beyond multicellular use of conserved cellular control loops. Any dataset of channel genes, regeneration, or learning in unicells can be described without a retained cognitive repertoire. The claim is therefore not separated from its non-cognitive rival by existing data.

operationalization: Shared molecules and similar feedback structure in morphogenesis and behaviour are expected if neural control was exapted from older physiological signalling, with no scaling of goals. No measurement distinguishes that exaptation from a pivot of collective intelligence along one continuum, so the outcome of a comparative survey would not confirm or refute the proposal.
obstacles: Goal and collective intelligence are not tied to one measurement that rivals must fail.
A continuum claim is compatible with both deep homology of signalling parts and a cognitive redescription of the same parts.
rationale: Phylogenies of ion channels and transmitters can show reuse of physiological machinery in nervous systems. They cannot show that evolution pivoted collective intelligence by enlarging homeostatic setpoints, because a non-cognitive exaptation account fits the same genes and the same behaviours. The proposal has no discriminating observation.

operationalization: For published developmental models with an explicit genotype-to-anatomy map, attempt to recover parameter or genotype changes that produce a specified large-scale anatomical change, and compare success with and without a known route for somatic information to reach the germline. Systematic failure of inversion in well-specified models would support computational irreversibility as a barrier; reliable inversion, or empirical cases where a known edit produces a chosen organ-scale trait, would count against unsolvability as the limit on Lamarckian inheritance.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public dynamical models of development whose invertibility can be probed as a restricted proxy

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: a fully specified generative map from evolved network to French-flag anatomy

obstacles: Unsolvability in general depends on the model class and is not read out of metazoan datasets.
Existing models cover a negligible fraction of real genotype-to-anatomy maps.
rationale: Inversion difficulty can be measured on public developmental models, which is analysis of a proxy. Those models do not establish that real morphogenesis is unsolvable or that this, rather than transmission to the germline, is what limits Lamarckian inheritance across metazoans. The claim's full scope is not in any dataset.

operationalization: In the public artificial-embryogeny model, compare the rate of fitness gain and the fraction of accepted changes in competency rules versus structural genes. Faster search and a shift toward competency edits would support a proxy in which evolution spends its effort on behaviour-shaping rules; equal or greater progress through structural edits would count against that proxy.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public simulations and saved runs contrasting hardwired and competent development, the nearest explicit search process

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: comparative gene repertoires for a weak proxy based on signalling versus structural genes

obstacles: The simulation searches a toy axial map, not the space of metazoan cell-behaviour rules.
Elevated evolution of signalling genes is compatible with ordinary selection on phenotypes and does not identify the search space.
rationale: The cited competency model is public, includes saved runs, and can show whether selection shifts onto competency parameters. That is a proxy for one sentence of a much broader claim about what evolution searches in metazoans. Sequence collections do not discriminate behaviour-shaping signals from the rest of the genome as the object of search.

operationalization: Compare public evolutionary runs that use a compressed generative encoding with otherwise matched direct encodings, and score robustness and success on environments not seen during selection. Higher novel-environment success for the generative encoding would support the architectural prediction; no difference, or a difference explained by parameter count alone, would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public indirect developmental layer between genotype and the phenotype that selection sees

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public ES-HyperNEAT system in which a CPPN is a compressed generator of the cell network

obstacles: The autoencoder analogy is not a unique encoding, so several implementations can be called confirmatory.
Robustness in a toy embryogeny does not show that real evolution is pushed to general-purpose problem solvers.
rationale: Indirect encodings in the two public models can be scored for performance off the training conditions, which tests a narrow version of the architectural claim. Neither model is a variational autoencoder of a metazoan genome, and success in those runs would not show that evolution is freed from over-training or that plasticity in organisms is produced by that compression.

operationalization: Relate measured gap-junction coupling, or a specific blockade, to the spatial scale of a patterning outcome and to whether a transient stimulus still alters a later regenerative choice. Pattern scale shrinking under blockade, and memory of a stimulus surviving only when coupling is intact, would support the scaling claim; pattern scale and stimulus memory unchanged by coupling would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus connexin expression and phenotype annotations, a molecular baseline rather than a coupling-versus-memory experiment

obstacles: Gap-junction blockers have off-target effects, and dye coupling is not memory or predictive capacity.
No public dataset pairs coupling strength with a later anatomical setpoint across tissues.
rationale: Blockade and dye-coupling experiments already published can speak to whether electrical coupling changes the scale of pattern, but they are scattered in papers rather than a downloadable table of memory radius against coupling. Xenbase covers gene annotations, not that functional pairing. Enlarged goal states are not distinguished from a change in physiological correlation length.

operationalization: Compare motility and collective behaviour of Xenopus embryonic epidermal cells dissociated from the embryo with intact embryonic epidermis. Self-motile aggregates formed from those cells, and absent while the cells remain in place, would support the explant result; failure to form motile constructs under the published dissociation protocol would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Reconfigurable organisms design code
candidate_datasets.role: public evolutionary design code for the Xenobot shapes; it does not hold the wet-lab motility recordings

obstacles: Ciliary motility used for mucus clearance in vivo can look like a novel behaviour once cells are free in culture.
Trial-level videos and counts sit in the original papers' supplements, not in an independent data repository.
rationale: The explant contrast is concrete and the design pipeline's code is public, but the biological outcome is documented as published experimental reports from the same research program rather than a reusable tracking dataset. Those reports can be checked for whether motile aggregates were produced. They do not isolate the neighbour signals supposed to suppress the behaviour, so the suppression clause stays partly untested.

operationalization: Date ion-channel and pump families on public bacterial and metazoan genomes and align that distribution with published biofilm electrical signalling. Channels and propagating ionic signals already present in biofilms would support early availability of the hardware; restriction of such signals to nervous systems would count against the timing.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: annotated ion-channel and pump sequences across bacteria and animals

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: public genomes for placing those families relative to biofilms and nervous systems

obstacles: Presence of a channel gene is not evidence that it was used to integrate information across a biofilm.
The purpose clause, that this is why brains use the same modality, is not a separate observable.
rationale: Public protein and genome collections can test whether the relevant electrical hardware is ancient and present in bacteria, which is the dating half of the statement. Published biofilm physiology is separate and not a single deposited time series here. Neither resource records an evolutionary discovery of information processing, as opposed to cells that happen to be electrically coupled.

operationalization: In Xenopus tadpoles, compare eye formation after misexpression of the specified ion channels that reproduce a facial voltage pattern in gut or tail, against the same sites after Pax6 delivery alone. Ectopic eyes at those sites after the voltage manipulation, and not after Pax6 there, would support the report; no ectopic eyes, or eyes induced equally by Pax6 outside the anterior neurectoderm, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: registry of Xenopus eye and ion-channel phenotypes and the papers that report them; animal-level voltage and eye tables are not a downloadable matrix

obstacles: The induction frequencies and voltage images are in the original papers' figures, not a public animal-level file.
Injected cells can recruit neighbours, so the competent tissue is not cleanly the injected territory alone.
rationale: Eye presence, injection site, and the Pax6 contrast are standard experimental variables, and the published Xenopus literature, indexed for this species in Xenbase, reports them. There is no open matrix of voltage pattern against organ outcome that an outside group can reprocess, and independent replication series are not a separate dataset. The test is therefore a reassessment of published measurements for this species, not a full reanalysis.

operationalization: Score visual learning in Xenopus tadpoles with native eyes prevented and one ectopic eye on the tail, and record whether that eye's axons enter the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain. Learning above the no-eye and extraocular-photoreception controls would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that survives removal of the ectopic eye, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus phenotype and literature registry for ectopic-eye experiments; trial-level training scores are not deposited there

obstacles: Extraocular light sensitivity can imitate vision unless the ectopic eye is covered or removed as a control.
The behavioural trials are published as summary performance, not as a public trial table.
rationale: The learning assay and the anatomical connection are concrete, and the 2013 experimental report gives published performance for this exact preparation. Those measurements can be reassessed against the stated controls, but they cannot be recomputed from raw choices, and Xenbase does not hold the trial file. The result is checkable as a published experiment, not as an open behavioural dataset.

operationalization: In polyploid newt kidney tubules, count cells per cross-section, cell size, and whether a single cell closes the lumen, compared with diploid tubules that use about eight to ten cells. A shift from a multicellular tube to one wrapped cell at higher ploidy would support the anatomical report; persistent multicellular tubes despite giant cells would refute it.
obstacles: The observations are mid-twentieth-century histological accounts, not a digital image archive.
Downward causation and the choice of cytoskeletal bending over cell-cell communication are interpretations of the same sections.
rationale: Cell number and lumen closure are measurable, and the classical newt literature reports them for this organ. There is no public image set from which the counts can be redone, so coverage is the published descriptions of one system. The goal-directed and downward-causation reading is not separated by those sections from a passive geometric consequence of enlarged cells.

operationalization: On any public model that contains ion-channel genotype, a bioelectric pattern, and an anatomical output, compare inversion error for the direct genotype-to-anatomy map with the two-step path through the bioelectric pattern. Lower error on both steps than on the direct map would support the decomposition; equal or worse error would refute it for that model.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public dynamical models that can be searched for maps linking physiology to pattern; few encode genotype, voltage, and anatomy together

obstacles: Almost no deposited model contains all three layers with an invertible map.
Easier inversion in a model is not evidence about the historical control problem faced by evolution.
rationale: The two-step inversion comparison is a definite numerical test on a model that has both layers. Public model repositories rarely encode genotype, voltage, and anatomy together, so only a proxy analysis is available. The claim about real bioelectric control and about engineers is not settled by that proxy.

operationalization: Align yeast plasma-membrane proton-pump sequences and structures with Xenopus V-ATPase subunits, and compare tadpole tail regeneration when the yeast pump is expressed in place of V-ATPase function. Absence of significant sequence and structural homology, together with rescue of regeneration and of the regenerative voltage, would support interchangeability of the voltage state; homology, or rescue without restoration of voltage, would count against voltage as the instructive variable.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: sequences of the yeast proton pump and vertebrate V-ATPase subunits for a homology test

candidate_datasets.name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
candidate_datasets.role: structures for the same proteins, to test the no-structural-homology clause

obstacles: The tail-regeneration rescue counts are in the original experimental paper, not in UniProt or the PDB.
A yeast pump could restore regeneration by changing pH independently of the voltage pattern the claim treats as the signal.
rationale: The homology half can be settled directly from public sequences and structures. The functional phenocopy is a specific Xenopus regeneration result published as experimental measurements, without a deposited animal-level regeneration file in these databases. Voltage as the coarse-grained instructive variable is supported only if the rescue is tied to the bioelectric state rather than to a side effect of proton pumping.

operationalization: Treat memory as a regenerative head number that stays altered after a brief physiological treatment is washed out, in animals whose genotype is the wild-type stock, and that can be reset by a later physiological treatment. Stable two-headed regeneration after a two-day treatment, reversible without a genetic change, would support multiple stored targets; immediate reversion after washout, or a mutation that co-segregates with head number, would refute it.
obstacles: Persistent drug, epigenetic marks, or microbiome changes can store the phenotype without a bioelectric target representation.
Head-number counts are in the experimental papers, not in a public individual-level file, and the lines have not been shown by a deposited genome to be free of mutations.
rationale: The memory operationalization is the right kind: a persistent change in regenerative outcome after a transient stimulus, with a reset. Published planarian experiments report that pattern for wild-type stocks. Those counts are not a reusable dataset, and several non-bioelectric stores fit the same persistence, so existing reports test the phenomenon only in part.

operationalization: Quantify head outlines of gap-junction-blocker-treated genetically wild-type Girardia dorotocephala and compute morphological distances to untreated heads of other planarian species, then place those species on a dated phylogeny. Treated heads falling nearer other species' shapes than their own controls, across divergence times on the order of 100 to 150 million years, would support the report; shapes that are only disrupted, or divergence times far from that range for the species actually compared, would count against the corresponding clause.

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: dated divergences among planarian lineages for the 100–150 million year clause; it does not contain the head outlines

obstacles: Head-shape measurements live in the 2015 paper's figures, not in TimeTree or a morphometric archive.
A generic dysmorphic head can be scored as species-like unless the distance to each species shape is pre-specified.
rationale: Shape distance and divergence time are both measurable, and TimeTree can check the temporal clause once the species pair is fixed. The shape data are the published images from one experiment, not an open landmark file, so an independent remasurement is limited. Species-specific recapitulation has to be separated from nonspecific disruption.

operationalization: Track ciliary beat direction and feeding after a 180-degree cortical rotation in Paramecium or a related ciliate, across asexual generations, and sequence the same lines. Inheritance of reversed beating with a genome that matches the unoperated stock would support cortical inheritance that the genome does not correct; loss of the reversal within a few fissions, or a fixed nuclear mutation, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Ciliate Genome Database
candidate_datasets.role: reference genomes for Paramecium and Tetrahymena; it does not include the surgically rotated lines

obstacles: The classical lines were not sequenced, so wild-type DNA is inferred from genetics rather than from a public genome of those cells.
The primary observations are journal descriptions from the 1960s onward, not a single downloadable pedigree.
rationale: Cortical rotation, inheritance across fissions, and failure of the nucleus to restore normal feeding are concrete and were reported repeatedly in the ciliate literature. Reference genomes exist, but not for the operated lines, so the wild-type-DNA clause cannot be rechecked from sequence. The anatomical inheritance can be assessed from the published experiments, with the limits of pre-genomic records.

operationalization: Reanalyze the Dugesia japonica barium RNA-seq with a pre-specified handful rule, for example fewer than 20 genes at FDR under 0.05 and a stated fold change, in heads that regenerated in BaCl2 versus controls. A count under that cutoff would support the transcriptional clause; a count of dozens or hundreds would refute a handful.

candidate_datasets.name: GEO series GSE98084
candidate_datasets.role: public RNA-seq of Dugesia japonica adapting to barium chloride, for a recount of differentially expressed genes

obstacles: A handful is undefined until a threshold is fixed, and the original paper used a stringent fold-change cutoff.
Pooled or few samples limit the stability of the gene list, and the anatomical time course is not in the expression matrix.
rationale: The expression half is directly in a public series and can be recounted with ordinary differential-expression methods. That recount can support or refute a small gene list, which is only part of the statement. Head loss and barium-insensitive regrowth, and the reading that cells thereby solved an unselected problem, are not variables in the count matrix and are not discriminated from a generic stress transcriptome.

operationalization: Rank species by an explicit regeneration score, a cancer-incidence measure, and a longevity measure, then test whether high regeneration predicts low cancer and long life after phylogenetic correction. A joint association in that direction would support the comparative pattern; regenerative taxa with high cancer or short life, or a pattern that vanishes under phylogeny and body size, would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge
candidate_datasets.role: species longevity records for the aging clause; it does not score regeneration or cancer

obstacles: Regeneration ability and comparative cancer rates are not in one open table and are biased by how hard tumors are to see in small aquatic animals.
Body size, phylogeny, and indeterminate growth confound any three-way association.
rationale: Longevity is tabulated for many species, so the aging arm has a real dataset, while regeneration and cancer resistance are scattered qualitative reports. A phylogenetically controlled test can be sketched for a subset of taxa and would be informative only with serious confounds. The expectation about undifferentiated cells and cancer is not a separate measured variable.

operationalization: In the public competency model, track the fraction of fitness-improving changes that alter competency parameters versus structural genes as competency is allowed to evolve. An increasing share of competency edits, and weaker selection on the structural genome, would support the ratchet inside that model; continued improvement mainly in structural genes would refute it there.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public code and pre-saved runs for hardwired, competent, and evolvable-competency populations

obstacles: The model uses a one-dimensional positional target, so its ratchet need not be the biological one.
Ordering planaria, salamanders, and mammals by degree of competency is not a variable in the saved runs.
rationale: The computational ratchet is re-runnable from a public repository that already stores simulation outputs, so that part can be confirmed or refuted by a standard reanalysis. The claim also ranks real lineages, and nothing in the repository or in a comparable open table measures their competency. The model result is a proxy for the evolutionary statement, not the whole of it.

operationalization: Search FlyBase, Mouse Genome Informatics, and the planarian literature for stable inherited strains whose anatomy differs from wild type in the absence of ongoing RNAi or drug treatment. Morphological mutant strains in flies and mice, and at least one published planarian strain of that kind, would refute the negative planarian clause; a documented absence of such planarian strains, with the only permanent abnormal lines being the bioelectric one-head and two-head forms, would support it as a statement about the public record.

candidate_datasets.name: FlyBase
candidate_datasets.role: catalog of Drosophila strains with abnormal morphology, the contrast class

candidate_datasets.name: Mouse Genome Informatics
candidate_datasets.role: catalog of mouse mutant alleles and phenotypes, the other contrast class

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: index of planarian genetics papers through which a stable morphological mutant strain would be found

obstacles: RNAi phenotypes and transient drug phenotypes are easy to mistake for mutant strains.
A literature search can refute the negative claim by finding a strain, but cannot prove that no unpublished strain exists.
Transgenesis attempts after the paper's publication can change the public record without a single dedicated database.
rationale: The contrast with flies and mice is directly queryable in phenotype databases, and planarian strain reports are public literature. That is enough to test a claim about what is known, including the bioelectric origin of the familiar two-headed lines. It is not a complete census of stocks, and the competency-ratchet explanation of the absence is not tested by the search.

operationalization: From the saved competent and hardwired populations, compare phenotypic variance among genotypes, escapes from local fitness plateaus, and whether a deleterious local displacement is corrected before fitness is scored. Lower phenotypic differences and more escapes under competency would support smoothing and more efficient search in the model; identical landscapes would refute it there.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public runs comparing evolvability of competent and hardwired embryos on a simple axial target

obstacles: The fitness landscape is a toy monotonic gradient, so local maxima of real development are not in the data.
Smoothing by competency is not separated, in organisms, from canalization by other mechanisms.
rationale: The model was built to compare hardwired and regulative development and its outputs are public, so the efficiency and masking effects can be recomputed. That tests the mechanism inside the stated simulation, which covers only a thin analogue of regulative evolution. Organismal fitness landscapes and the hypothetical mouth correction are not in those files.

operationalization: Estimate the fraction of mutations that are phenotypically silent under normal development and revealed under a perturbation, in a system with regulative development, and compare with a direct genotype-to-phenotype encoding if one is available. A larger silent pool that later becomes visible would support cryptic variation produced by buffering; absence of that pool, or a pool explained by protein chaperones rather than developmental correction, would count against the competency-specific version.

candidate_datasets.name: FlyBase
candidate_datasets.role: alleles and phenotype annotations for Drosophila cryptic-variation and capacitor experiments, a partial biological analogue

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public comparison of how developmental correction hides structural-gene differences from selection

obstacles: Cryptic variation is well documented for chaperones and redundancy, which are rivals to multiscale competency.
FlyBase does not record a pool of mutations buffered specifically by anatomical error correction.
rationale: Cryptic genetic variation can be surveyed in Drosophila resources, and the competency model can show mutations hidden from selection by a developmental layer. Those are partial proxies. They do not identify multiscale competency, as opposed to other buffering, as the cause of a dormant pool that evolution later exploits.

operationalization: Measure habituation as reduced crossing of a noxious region after repeated exposure, recovered by a dishabituation control, and measure growth direction toward inert objects that differ in mass. Reduced withdrawal plus reliable growth toward the heavier object would support the learning and decision results; no change, or growth explained by a chemical cue correlated with mass, would count against them.
obstacles: Raw trajectories are spread across papers and video supplements, not one archive.
Habituation protocols differ, and some replications have been disputed.
Growth toward mass can be a biomechanical taxis without a decision variable.
rationale: Habituation and growth direction are standard measurements, and several independent Physarum papers report them, so a restricted test can be assembled from published results. There is no single open trajectory archive, and the mass result in particular needs its controls rechecked from the source paper. The identification of behaviour with morphological change is true of this organism's mode of movement and does not further discriminate the learning result.

operationalization: Train intact planarians on a specified task, cut off tails, let the tails regenerate a brain, and compare task performance with naive regenerated controls and with animals trained after regeneration. Retention above both controls would support memory in the new brain; performance explained by residual tissue, sensitization, or experimenter cueing would refute it.
obstacles: McConnell's mid-century protocols are widely regarded as poorly controlled, and raw trial sheets are not public.
The modern Dugesia japonica result is one laboratory's published summary, without a deposited trial table.
rationale: Retention after regeneration is a clear behavioural contrast, and two published studies report it. Their measurements can be reassessed only at the level of published summaries, and the older study is confounded. Existing reports therefore test the phenomenon partially and do not settle whether the new brain received an imprint of the original training.

operationalization: In Xenopus tadpoles with no primary eyes and one tail eye, score visually guided learning and trace axons from that eye. Learning that requires the tail eye, with axons entering the spinal cord, would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that remains after the tail eye is removed, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus experiment and phenotype registry pointing to the ectopic-eye study; it does not store the learning trials

obstacles: Published performance is a summary, not trial-level choices.
Extraocular photoreception is the main rival and has to be read off the paper's controls.
rationale: This is the same preparation as the behavioural tail-eye result, with a narrower endpoint: vision and a spinal connection. The experimental paper publishes those outcomes for this scope. They can be checked against the described controls and cannot be recomputed from an open trial file.

operationalization: In paired transcriptome and electrophysiology profiles, predict resting or firing features from transcript levels and ask whether distinct channel sets map to the same electrical phenotype. Prediction no better than a permutation null, or identical transcriptomes with different voltage states, would support unreadability; accurate prediction of the electrical phenotype from transcripts or proteins would refute a strict reading.

candidate_datasets.name: Allen Brain Cell Types
candidate_datasets.role: public patch-seq and electrophysiology for mammalian cortical neurons, pairing transcripts with electrical features

obstacles: The atlas covers spiking neurons, not the slow developmental voltage patterns the surrounding argument is about.
A snapshot cannot test history dependence, and proteins are not paired with voltage in this resource.
rationale: Paired gene expression and electrophysiology are public for a large set of neurons and can show how much electrical phenotype is readable from transcripts. That tests the neural subset and can refute an absolute version of unreadability. It does not cover non-neural bioelectric maps, proteomics, or the history dependence the mechanism invokes, so the claim's full scope stays only partly tested.

operationalization: Gap-junction and ion-channel coupling that coordinates cells over a larger distance and a longer time is predicted equally by ordinary bioelectric physiology. No observation distinguishes that coordination from a cognitive glue that binds cellular goals into a larger cognitive light cone, in brain or non-brain tissue.
obstacles: Cognitive glue, goal-directedness, and cognitive light cone do not fix a single measurement.
Any physiological dataset offered as support is also a non-cognitive description of the same facts.
rationale: Tissue-scale bioelectric coupling is measurable, and that measurement does not require the cognitive vocabulary. The claim's extra content, that these networks are a cognitive glue enlarging a light cone of goals, is not separated from physiological integration by any available observation. The statement is therefore not empirically resolvable as opposed to its non-cognitive restatement.

operationalization: Place ion-channel, gap-junction, and neurotransmitter-synthesis genes on a dated tree of animals and ask whether they predate nervous systems, and compare the timescale of non-neural voltage events with synaptic spikes. Earlier origins and a shift from slow spatial patterns to millisecond spikes would support reuse and speed-up; origins only inside nervous systems would count against the historical premise.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: protein families for channels, connexins and innexins, and transmitter-related enzymes

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: divergence times against which those families can be compared with the origin of nervous systems

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: public genomes of early-branching animals and outgroups for presence and absence

obstacles: An ancient gene family can predate nervous systems without having been used for morphogenesis.
The speed comparison is between living physiological regimes, not a recorded evolutionary transition.
rationale: Public sequences and divergence times can test whether the named components are older than brains, which is the conservation premise behind the pivot. They cannot show original use in morphospace, nor that neuroscience tools work in the body because of that history. The historical purpose remains an inference beyond the phylogenetic data.

operationalization: Count axolotl forelimbs that reach digits after one through five amputations in the same plane, and contrast gene expression in limbs that have stopped with first-amputation controls. A progressive drop in completed regenerates would support the empirical decline, and no drop would refute it; expression dominated by a persistent wound-healing or amphiregulin response would favour scarring over habituation of an anatomical setpoint.

candidate_datasets.name: GEO series GSE103087
candidate_datasets.role: RNA-seq of axolotl limbs that failed after repeated amputation versus normally regenerating controls

obstacles: The success-versus-amputation curve is in the paper's figures; the expression series is only the failed-versus-control contrast at one stage.
Fibrosis and elevated amphiregulin, the study's own mechanism, mimic giving up on a target morphology.
rationale: Repeated-amputation outcomes and a matching expression series are public enough to test whether regeneration declines and whether the decline looks like a wound-healing program. That can confirm the empirical stop and can favour a rival to pattern-memory habituation. It does not measure a stored anatomical setpoint being edited by experience, and it covers axolotl forelimbs rather than regenerating animals generally.

operationalization: Record the position of an experimental or accidental injury on a deer antler and the position of any extra branch in subsequent years after the rack is shed. Coincidence of the ectopic branch with the old injury site across years would support the positional memory; failure of the site to recur, or recurrence explained by a permanent pedicle scar visible in the scalp, would count against a memory held only as information about past damage.
obstacles: The reports are small historical case series, not a public table of injury coordinates and later racks.
A structural scar in the pedicle can place the next branch without a stored 3D memory.
rationale: Injury site and later branch position are measurable, but no open dataset of antler injuries and subsequent morphology exists to analyze. The published cases are narrative observations. Distinguishing a remembered target from a persistent local scar would require new paired records, or at least a compiled individual-level series that is not currently public.

operationalization: After a transient bioelectric or gap-junction treatment, cut fragments in later rounds with no further drug and record head number, plus a reset cohort returned to one head by a second manipulation. Two-headed regenerates across rounds, reversed by the reset and not by washout alone, would support a stored target; return to one head as soon as the drug is gone, or a heritable mutation, would refute it.
obstacles: Round-by-round head counts are in the experimental papers, not a deposited lineage table.
A persistent non-genetic store other than the bioelectric circuit, including bacteria, can keep the two-headed outcome.
rationale: Persistence across amputations and experimental reset are a direct test of a modifiable regenerative target, and the published planarian studies report both. The animal-level lineages are not an open dataset, so the test is a reassessment of those reports. Other stable physiological stores remain live alternatives on the existing evidence.

operationalization: Hold genotype fixed, by wild-type stock plus reversibility or by sequencing, and record regenerative head number after different physiological histories. One, two, and zero heads from the same genotype would support head number not being a direct function of the genome; a genetic variant necessary for each deviant head number would refute it.
obstacles: Wild-type is usually inferred from stock history and reversibility, not from deposited genomes of the zero- and two-headed animals.
History can include microbiome and chromatin changes that are still encoded outcomes of the genome's regulatory capacities.
rationale: Whether head number varies at a fixed genotype is an empirical contrast, and the published physiological manipulations report one-, two-, and zero-headed outcomes from wild-type stocks. Those results are paper-level measurements, not a sequence-plus-phenotype matrix. The software metaphor adds no further observable beyond that genotype-phenotype dissociation.

operationalization: On a phylogeny, find morphology shifts that match a phenotype first produced by a bioelectric manipulation, and ask whether ion-channel substitutions were fixed afterward and then produce the phenotype without the manipulation. That order would support genetic assimilation; channel changes with no such plastic precursor, or plastic phenotypes that were never genetically fixed, would count against it as an important route to body plans.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: ion-channel sequences that could be compared across lineages; they do not record bioelectric phenotypes or assimilation events

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: divergence times for body-plan splits, without the physiological history of those splits

obstacles: No dataset records a bioelectrically induced phenotype and a later genetic fixation of that phenotype.
Likely importance and the Baldwin-effect analogy are not decided by channel sequence divergence.
rationale: Sequences and divergence times are public, but the decisive variables are a plastic bioelectric phenotype and its later genetic assimilation, which are not in those databases. A comparative test is definable and cannot be run on existing open data. The claim stays a historical likelihood rather than a result those resources can confirm or refute.

operationalization: Regenerate Dugesia japonica fragments exposed to the endogenous Aquitalea isolate or to indole, against microbiome-depleted controls, and score permanent two-headed anatomy. Two-headed animals specifically under the bacterium or indole, and not under depletion alone, would support hijacking of the default pattern; no change in head number would refute it.
obstacles: The RNA-seq mentioned with the indole treatment was not found as a public series, and head-number counts are in the paper.
Indole has several host effects, so a two-headed outcome need not mean the morphogenetic circuit was overridden in the same way as a bioelectric rewrite.
rationale: Head number under a defined bacterial treatment is a direct experimental endpoint, and the 2020 paper reports it for this commensal and for indole. Those measurements are not a deposited count table or expression series that can be reprocessed. The result can be reassessed from the publication and cannot be recomputed from open raw data.

operationalization: In anatomically one-headed planarians, compare the bioelectric pattern and gene-expression profile with later head number after an experimental cut. A two-headed voltage pattern before injury, with ordinary anatomy and ordinary expression, that predicts two heads after the cut, would support a pattern that is not a readout of current anatomy; a voltage pattern that matches current head number would refute that dissociation.
obstacles: Voltage images and expression comparisons are in the source paper's figures, not a public image and count matrix.
Predicting the regenerative outcome is expected of any causal prepattern, with or without memory of a counterfactual target.
rationale: The dissociation among current anatomy, voltage pattern, expression, and later head number is a real empirical test and is what the cited experiment reports. Those data are not an open, reanalyzable set. Calling the pattern a counterfactual memory does not add a measurement that a non-representational cause of the later anatomy would fail.

operationalization: For fragments from ion-channel-drug-treated cryptic worms, record head number at each successive regeneration without further drug and test whether the two outcomes occur as draws rather than as a fixed lineage state. Frequencies near a stable mixture, with individual lines flipping, would support bistable recall; each fragment locking to one morphology, or flipping only while the drug remains, would refute it.
obstacles: Per-fragment outcome sequences are not a public table, so published proportions could hide stable subclasses.
Environmental noise between cuts can imitate a bistable circuit.
rationale: Stochastic one-head versus two-head outcomes across rounds are countable, and the cryptic-worm experiments report that mixture after a physiological treatment. The lineage sequences needed to separate true flipping from a mixture of stable animals are not deposited. Existing published proportions therefore test the result only in part.
